clue.text: Extra work gives one the edge

definitions.text: Extra work gives one the edge

parts.words: Extra work gives one the edge
parts.note: a second job on the side of the main one, thought of as putting the worker at the edge of the field of play

explanation.surface: Putting in additional hours is what gets you ahead of your rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives one the edge' sounds like gaining an advantage; read literally it is being put on the edge, the touchline, of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary occupation pursued alongside a main job; as a verb it also means pushing someone to the margins.

clue.text: Bristling, but sees to renovation

indicators.note: a renovation rebuilds something, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone bristles with irritation but still attends to the building works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovation' rearranges the letters of SEES TO; 'but' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical and zoological term for covered with stiff hairs or bristles.

clue.text: American state that gathers facts about a stunning blow

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: KO is a knockout, a blow that stuns

explanation.surface: A US state compiles statistics about a knockout punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DATA round KO; 'that gathers' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: North and South are both US states, collectively the Dakotas.

clue.text: How the banquet indulged in flattery

definitions.meaning: a banquet is provided or arranged for guests, as a feast is put on
laying it on thick means praising excessively

explanation.surface: A feast was arranged and its host was buttered up with compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is provided for guests; the phrase also means piling on praise, as in laying it on thick.

clue.text: Free credit offer failing to excite enthusiasm

definitions.meaning: a loan deal where the borrower pays nothing extra
attracting nobody's attention or curiosity

explanation.surface: A zero-charge loan deal leaves customers cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Loans charging nothing extra are advertised this way; the same words say that nobody is curious.

clue.text: Nippers who work diligently at selling their wares

definitions.meaning: nippers are gripping tools with jaws

definitions.text: who work diligently at selling their wares
definitions.meaning: to ply a trade is to work at it steadily, so traders who do so are those who ply

explanation.surface: Young children busily hawk goods at market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nippers' suggests children; here it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Gripping hand tools are nippers; those who ply their trade are literally plyers.

clue.text: Final African republic survived longer than the others

parts.note: Togo is a republic in West Africa

explanation.surface: The final African republic outlasted all its neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever remains when everyone else has left or died is the final one standing.

clue.text: Equally applicable to all parts

definitions.meaning: as in '... as good', meaning just as good
the whole of something, each piece of it

explanation.surface: A rule applies in the same way to every component.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'quite as' before an adjective, and literally the whole of something.

clue.text: Spy noses out summaries of plots

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A secret agent sniffs out outlines of conspiracies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SPY NOSES; 'plots' suggests conspiracies but means stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief outlines of a story's events, as printed for a film or novel.

clue.text: Understand how a slimmer should remodel her skirt

definitions.meaning: to absorb or grasp information

definitions.text: how a slimmer should remodel her skirt
definitions.meaning: after losing weight, a skirt is made narrower at the seams

explanation.surface: A dieter must grasp that her clothes need altering.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to grasp something mentally, and also to make a garment narrower.

clue.text: A forbidding order to go back in the navy

definitions.text: order to go back in the navy

explanation.surface: A naval command is barked out strictly.
explanation.definitionFit: A command for a ship to move backwards, towards the rear.

clue.text: Begin a journey located by a Scottish firth

parts.note: a thing located somewhere is set there
the Firth of Forth is an estuary in Scotland near Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A traveller departs from a spot on a Scottish estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out or depart on a trip.

clue.text: Don't go to bed put on your corsets!

definitions.meaning: to remain awake late
corsets are called stays, so wearing them holds you up

explanation.surface: A mother tells someone to stay awake and get dressed in underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain awake past bedtime; corsets are stays, and they hold the figure firm.

clue.text: Pretty young lass is a little down

definitions.meaning: dated slang for an attractive girl
down is soft fluff, so a small piece of it

explanation.surface: An attractive girl is feeling slightly depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like sadness; here it is soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for an attractive young woman, and literally a small wisp of soft feathers.

clue.text: The fatiguing length of a court case

definitions.text: The fatiguing length of a court case

parts.words: The fatiguing length of a court case
parts.note: a period that wears you out, and also the period during which a defendant is being tried

explanation.surface: A lengthy court hearing exhausts everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult period, punningly the period spent being tried in court.

clue.text: LSD experiment provides the best proof

definitions.meaning: LSD is the drug known as acid, so a trial of it
a decisive check of worth, from testing gold with nitric acid

explanation.surface: A drug trial offers the most convincing evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provides' is just a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclusive trial of value, originally gold tested with acid; also literally a trial of the drug.

clue.text: Wine in a condition to be carried

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, meaning able to be carried

parts.note: able means in a fit condition to do something

explanation.surface: The wine is fit to be transported.
explanation.definitionFit: Light enough to be lifted and moved about easily.

clue.text: Drive as fast as you can to permit one journey

definitions.text: Drive as fast as you can

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A driver floors the accelerator to allow a single trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for going at full speed, giving an engine free rein.

clue.text: Union policy apparently put the retailer out of business

definitions.meaning: a workplace where only trade union members may be employed

definitions.text: apparently put the retailer out of business
definitions.meaning: a shut store, read literally

explanation.surface: Union rules seem to have bankrupted a shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm where membership of a trade union is compulsory; literally a store that has ceased trading.

clue.text: Last month a politician had to do a bunk

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, is the last month of the year
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: In December an MP had to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do a bunk' is British slang for running off; 'had to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave suddenly or secretly, to abscond.

clue.text: Avant garde exit

definitions.meaning: radically experimental or unconventional
a way to leave a place

explanation.surface: An experimental artist leaves the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for highly unconventional, and the British signage for an exit route.

clue.text: Grab a lot of eggs

definitions.meaning: to seize tightly
a set of eggs laid at one time

explanation.surface: Someone snatches a batch of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize hold; also a set of eggs laid and hatched together.

clue.text: Dock feature

definitions.meaning: to dock an animal is to cut off its tail
a particular item or point

explanation.surface: A harbour has a notable characteristic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a harbour; it is the verb to cut short a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally to remove a tail, as docking does; also an individual feature or particular.

clue.text: Last despite everything

definitions.meaning: following every other one, at the end
nevertheless, in spite of what was said

explanation.surface: The final word: regardless of all that happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally behind every other one, so last; idiomatically it means nevertheless.

clue.text: Invitation Noah gave to eastern physician touching his boat

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Noah calls a doctor from the East aboard his vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An instruction to go aboard a ship, as Noah bid the animals.

clue.text: Distressed by gossip

definitions.meaning: upset, troubled
a rumour spread around is circulated by gossip

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by tittle-tattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Means upset or inconvenienced, and spread around, as a rumour is.

clue.text: I upset contrived business connections

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits to wrecking some carefully arranged commercial links.
explanation.definitionFit: Commercial links or mergers between firms.

clue.text: Like a wide, badly tuned instrument

definitions.meaning: in cricket a wide is a delivery too far from the batsman, so off the playing strip
an instrument sounding out of tune

explanation.surface: A badly tuned instrument is compared to an errant cricket ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide in cricket is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach, penalised by an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally away from the strip of cricket turf, and also out of tune.
